links.reason: Line 13 இரந்தோர்க்கு ஈயாது ஈட்டியோன் பொருள்போல் makes the miser's wealth the vehicle for unspent beauty (யாய் ஓம்பிய நலனே), while Kural 1007 makes a beautiful woman growing old alone (மிகநலம் பெற்றாள் தமியள்மூத்து) the vehicle for ungiven wealth. The reversal of tenor and vehicle is real and is something neither verse shows alone.

In 51 புணர்வது (l.10) has the wealth (பொருட்பிணி) as its subject: wealth is gained only by parting; in 1155 புணர்வு is union with the lover. The pairing rests on one word used in two senses; the 'both sides of one exchange' in teaches is the proposer's construction, though both poems do weigh parting against staying.

Both turn on நல்கூர்ந்த (331 l.3 நனிநல் கூர்ந்தனன்; 219 நல்கூர்ந்தானாதல்) and the poor man who still gives is a real match. But the note's 'unable to do what he should' is the commentator's reading; on the plain words செய்யாது அமைகலா ஆறு (cannot rest without doing) the Kural agrees with 331 rather than being qualified by it.

Pazhaiyan is named in both (326 l.11-12 போஒர் கிழவோன் பழையன் ஓக்கிய வேல்; 44 l.11 பழையன் பட்டென), a real puram-name link. But in 44 his fall belongs to the chain praising Chenni whose Azhumbil measures the wife's town; it is not used for 'the scale of a war that keeps a husband from home', so teaches misdescribes 44.

139 l.10 கனிபதம் பார்க்கும் காலையன்றே and l.12-14 (சாதல் அஞ்சாய் ... ஒருநாள் அருஞ்சமம் வருகுவதாயின்) argue for giving now because death may come, which is Naladiyar 5's பின்னாவதென்று பிடித்திரா ... கூற்றம். The difference (the bard's troupe loses in 139, the giver's fate in the Naladiyar) is what teaches names.
links.text_issue: Line 11 ஈதல் ஆனான் வேந்தே is hard to construe; the reading does not depend on it.

links.reason: 168 l.6-7 கொடைக்கடன் ஏன்ற கோடா நெஞ்சின் உதியன் அட்டில் is a real allusion to a giver's kitchen. But Purananuru 2 never names Udhiyan; the name is only in the colophon (பெருஞ்சோற்று உதியன்), and l.16 பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய் does not say to the armies. 'Stock measure of uproar' generalises from one simile.

Both name the battle: 19 l.17 எழுவர் நல்வலங் கடந்தோய் at தலையாலங் கானத்து, 36 l.14 and l.20 ஆலங் கானத்து ... எழுவர் நல்வலம் அடங்க. 36 takes only the victors' shout (வென்றிகொள் வீரர் ஆர்ப்பு) for the gossip, while 19 keeps மூதில் பெண்டிர் கசிந்து அழ; the contrast in use is real, though the mothers' tears in 19 are mixed with pride.

The wording matches closely: 10 l.4 ஒப்ப நாடி அத்தக ஒறுத்தி against 561 தக்காங்கு நாடி ... ஒத்தாங்கு ஒறுப்பது. 10 l.5-6 (வந்து அடி பொருந்தி ... தண்டமும் தணிதி) adds the softened penalty the couplet lacks, so teaches is accurate and hedged.

The images differ (ஞெலிகோல் and its கனைஎரி against கொக்கு and its குத்து), so this is not a shared image; what is shared is the pattern of one thing in two states with வல்லன் / பருவத்து timing. The point that the fire is already in the stick, so restraint is stored force, is true and would make this sound as develops.

The child's small hand in food is the same image in the same words: 188 l.3 சிறுகை நீட்டி and l.4 துழந்தும், Kural 64 சிறுகை அளாவிய கூழ். 64 makes it sweeter than amrita, and 188 makes its absence the verdict பயக்குறை இல்லை, so the difference in use is real.

Thithiyan of Pothiyil is named in both (322 l.8 திதியன், l.14 புகலரும் பொதியில்; 25 l.20 பொதியிற் செல்வன் பொலந்தேர்த் திதியன்). 322 uses the hill's inaccessibility for the girl and 25 his music (இன்இசை இயத்தின்) for the falls of the man's road. 'Opposite uses' overstates two unrelated similes, and the general claim about puram places is thin.

The name and epithet match (158 l.5 கொல்லி ஆண்ட வல்வில் ஓரி; 152 l.6 வல்வில் வேட்டம், l.12 ஓரி, l.31 கொல்லிப் பொருநன்). But the claim that the roll-call assumed an audience that knew the separate poems is not shown by the Tamil, and an epithet shared with a hunt story is a name link, not a development.

Ezhil hill is in both (345 l.7 ஏழில் குன்றத்து; 349 l.9 எழிற் குன்றத்து), and so is கருங்கால் வேங்கை, which the note misses. But in 345 the hill is where the couple would wear vengai before he leaves, not on his road, and its poet got horses by the grace of கான்அமர் செல்வி, not from a patron, so 'known through its patron's gifts' and 'the husband's road' misdescribe 345.

Both rest on the same refusal: 201 l.12-14 சோழர் வெண்ணெல் வைப்பின் நல்நாடு பெறினும் ஆண்டு அமைந்து உறைகுநர் அல்லர; 213 l.17-19 ஆன்றோர் அரும்பெறல் உலகம் அமிழ்தொடு பெறினும் ... நீடலோ இலரே. Pushing the prize from a kingdom to the world of the worthy, and measuring love by what he refuses, is accurate and specific.

Nannan with a chariot is in both (173 l.16 இயல்தேர் நன்னன்; 151 l.7-8 பொலந்தேர் நன்னன் மருகன்), so the name link is real. But in 151 the shut door (பாடுநர்க்கு அடைத்த கதவின்) belongs to the descendant's hill (நும் மால்வரை), not to Nannan, and 173's range is not drawn as dangerous; 'blame in one genre' is not what 151 says of Nannan.

669 asks for persistence in a joy-yielding task despite pain (துன்பம் உறவரினும் செய்க); 628 says the one who does not crave pleasure and counts pain natural does not suffer (இன்பம் விழையான்). Both accept pain, and they address different things, a task's fruit and personal craving, which is a difference of situation, not a conflict. The teaches line itself concedes this and teaches nothing.

The key word is shared: 121 l.3 வரிசை அறிதலோ அரிதே; 140 l.5-6 தான் பிற வரிசை அறிதலின் தன்னும் தூக்கி. 140 does measure the gift by the giver's own standing (an elephant for a request for rice), so the two-way sense of வரிசை in teaches is accurate.

159 l.22-25 refuses a grudging gift even of an elephant (தவிர்ந்துவிடு பரிசில் கொள்ளலென்) and accepts a kunri seed given gladly (உவந்து நீ இன்புற விடுதி யாயின்), after describing the starving household. Kural 1057's joy at இகழ்ந்தெள்ளாது ஈவார் becomes in 159 a condition of acceptance. That is a real development, though 'grudging' (தவிர்ந்துவிடு) is not quite the Kural's 'scornful'.

The seed links them: Kural 85 வித்தும் இடல்வேண்டும் கொல்லோ; 333 l.12 குரல்உணங்கு விதைத்தினை உரல்வாய்ப் பெய்து after all the millet went to suppliants (l.9-10). The maxim's rhetorical confidence that the host needs no seed is met by a poem where hospitality has consumed it.
links.text_issue: Lines 14-15 are lacunose; the link does not depend on them.

links.reason: 101 l.2-3 quotes 'நன்றுசெய் மருங்கில் தீதுஇல்' as a தொன்றுபடு பழமொழி and asks if it has failed (இன்றுபொய்த்தன்றுகொல்), since she did no wrong (முனிதகு பண்பு யாம் செய்தன்றோ இலமே). Kural 210 is close but not 'the same rule': it promises no ruin to one who does no evil (தீவினை செய்யான்), not reward for doing good. The tension holds on her reading, but the note overstates the identity.

The two criteria match: 40 l.9 இன்சொல் எண்பதத்தை ஆகுமதி; 386 காட்சிக்கு எளியன் கடுஞ்சொல்லன் அல்லன். Both also tie them to fame (40 l.6-7 புகழ் பாடுவோர் பொலிவு தோன்ற; 386 மீக்கூறும்), so the claim that the couplet's criteria were the bard's counsel is specific and supported.

Both have the bard's large kin (370 l.3 இரும்பே ரொக்கற்கு, starving; 378 l.13 இலம்பாடு உழந்தஎன் இரும்பேர் ஒக்கல், then jewelled), and the colophons give the same poet and patron. But இரும்பேர் ஒக்கல் is a stock bardic phrase, and 'before and after of one family' and 'the bard's rise' are built from the colophon, not shown by the two poems.

Both name Pulli's Venkatam (83 l.9-10 புல்லி ... வேங்கடம் கழியினும்; 61 l.12-13 மாவண் புல்லி விழவுடை விழுச்சீர் வேங்கடம் பெறினும்), and both describe its toddy-barter people (நறவுநொடை, 83 l.8, 61 l.10). It is used as a prize too small to keep him in 61 and as a distance her virtues cross in 83 (சேயர் என்னாது); teaches is accurate.

47 says the bard's life harms no one (பிறர்க்குத் தீதறிந்தன்றோ இன்றே), and Kural 586 tells the king to use spies in renunciants' guise (துறந்தார் படிவத்தர்). Neither verse says anything about the other's subject; the conflict exists only if we import a suspicion of spying that 47 never names, which comes from the traditional story, not the poem.

Both turn on the mother's pride and the word ஈன்ற (86 l.5 ஈன்ற வயிறோ இதுவே; 69 ஈன்ற பொழுதின்). But 86 says the son will appear on the battlefield (தோன்றுவன் மாதோ போர்க்களத்தானே), not that he will die, so 'a warrior's death' in teaches is not in the poem, and what is left is the shared topic of a mother's pride.

1138 says love breaks secrecy and comes into the open (மறையிறந்து மன்று படும்); in 52 the pallor is already visible (ஆய்மலர் உண்கண் பசலை), yet the heroine forbids naming it as காம நோய் even at the cost of her life (இன்உயிர் கழிவது ஆயினும்). The split between bodily disclosure and the refusal to name it is a real sharpening, though the colophon expects the friend to disclose anyway.

Kazhuvul's Kaamur is in both: 365 l.12-14 கழுவுள் காமூர் ... பூதம் தந்த பொரியரை வேங்கைத் தண்கமழ் புதுமலர் for the girl's hair, and 135 l.12-14 ஈர்-எழு வேளிர் இயந்துஒருங்கு எறிந்த கழுவுள் காமூர் போலக் கலங்கின்று for her shaken heart. One place serving fragrance and siege is accurately stated.

72 l.10-12 stakes the people's tears and blame (கொடியன்எம் இறை எனக் கண்ணீர் பரப்பிக் குடிபழி தூற்றும் கோலேன் ஆகுக) on the king's own failure; Kural 555 makes the tears of the afflicted (அழுதகண்ணீர்) what wears away wealth. 72 also stakes poverty (இரப்போர்க்கு ஈயா இன்மை), which fits. 'The worst penalty' slightly overstates one of three stakes.

Pannan of Sirukudi is in both (388 l.4 சிறுகுடி கிழான் பண்ணன்; 54 l.13-14 தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் பண்ணன் சிறுகுடி), a real puram name in akam. But the note misdescribes 54: the gooseberry of Pannan's garden is a taste simile for the wife's sweet prattle (நீர்குடி சுவையின் தீவிய மிழற்றி), not a landmark that sets the homecoming.

61 l.1-2 'நோற்றோர் மன்ற தாமே கூற்றம் கோளுற விளியார் பிறர்கொள விளிந்தோர்' is the belief behind 93's rite of cutting a body that died of sickness (நோய்ப்பால் விளிந்த யாக்கை ... வாள்போழ்ந்து) so it goes where battle-slain heroes go. The same creed shows up as a rite in one poem and as a saying that sends a man out for wealth in the other, which is specific and true.

Both foster mothers set the flight against a home celebration: 397 l.3-4 முழவுமுகம் புலரா விழவுடை வியனகர் மணனிடை யாகக் கொள்ளான் blames the youth, and 385 l.6-7 நன்மாண் விழவில் தகரம் மண்ணி யாம்பல புணர்ப்பச் சொல்லாள் dwells on the girl's silence. The difference in where the blame falls is accurate.
links.text_issue: Both verses are flagged uncertain; 397 line 2 is hard to construe.

links.reason: The exact phrase தூவெள் அறுவை (286 l.5 தூவெள் அறுவை போர்ப்பித்திலதே; 291 l.2 தூவெள் அறுவை மாயோன்) links a mother's line to a fallen warrior under the cloth. Using 291 to fix 286's last line as the shroud of the dead is a sound use of the parallel, and teaches allows for both readings of the negative.

The verbal match is close: 274 l.3 மேல்வரும் களிற்றொடு வேல்துரந்து and l.7 மெய்க்கொண்டனனே; 774 கைவேல் களிற்றொடு போக்கி ... மெய்வேல் பறியா நகும். The same scene of a spear sent with the elephant and the body taking the next blow is real. 'The chapter was built on stock episodes' generalises from one pair.
links.text_issue: 274 lines 6-7 leave the object of தழீஇ unstated.

links.reason: 379 l.11-12 (நின் கிணைவன் கூறக் கேட்டதற் கொண்டும்) does show a poet set on the road by another drummer's report, and 376 l.17-18 a drummer who never begs again. But the colophons give different patrons (ஓய்மான் வில்லியாதன், ஓய்மான் நல்லியாதன்), which the note blurs as 'an Oymaan chief', so 'the patron's advertisement' joins two patrons into one.
links.text_issue: 379 line 14 is broken and line 8 obscure.

links.reason: Evvi is in both (24 l.18 ஒம்பா ஈகை மாவேள் எவ்வி; 366 l.12 பொலம்பூண் எவ்வி), and 366's brawl scene with toddy given to the நுளையர் is accurately described. But the note leaves out that 24 names Evvi's Mizhalai among the Pandya's gains (l.19-22 மிழலையொடு ... தந்த), so the puram poem records his defeat, not a fame for protection.

Kolli is in both (338 l.13-15 பொறையன் ... கொல்லி போலத் தவாஅலியரே நட்பே; 209 l.12-16 ஓரிக் கொன்று சேரலர்க்கு ஈத்த ... கொல்லி). But 209 itself uses Kolli for permanence (நிலைபெறு கடவுள் ஆக்கிய பாவை), so the pair agrees. The irony in teaches, a permanence bought by a killing, is imposed on 338 and is not in either poem's use.

The sceptre-and-rain doctrine is shared: 117 l.6-7 கோஒல் செம்மையின் ... பெயல் பிழைப்பு அறியா; 545 இயல்புளிக் கோலோச்சும் மன்னவன் நாட்ட பெயலும். Setting it above the drought omens (l.1-2) is a real addition. But neither the poem nor its colophon (patron: -) names Pari, so 'grants it to a hill chief' rests on tradition, and 545's மன்னவன் need not mean only crowned kings.

The figure is shared in nearly the same words: 261 l.17-18 கொய்ம்மழித் தலையொடு ... கழிகலம் மகடூஉப் போல for the bereft house; 280 l.11-14 மண்ணுறு மழித்தலை ... கழிகல மகளிர் போல for the wife's own coming state. The shift from an image for a house to a foreseen fate for the speaker is accurate.

Both have a husband held by the king's war: 24 l.10-18 sets தம்ஊரோளே against யாமே ... வேந்தன் பாசறையேமே, and 1268 says வென்றீக வேந்தன் மனைகலந்து மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து. But 24 voices no wish for victory or for an evening feast; reading it as the vigil that produces the couplet's wish adds what neither says. This is the same situation, not a development.

The cluster is shared: பீர் pallor (135 l.2; 45 l.7), ஆதிமந்தி with பேதுற்று (135 l.5-6; 45 l.14), and a siege simile (135 l.12-13 Kamur; 45 l.17-18 உடைமதில் ஓர் அரண்). Both also have காடு இறந்தனரே காதலர் (135 l.10; 45 l.6), which the note misses. A ready set of lament images used by two poets is shown.

The closing formula matches (328 l.14 வாழையஞ் சிலம்பிற் றுஞ்சும்; 332 l.9 வாழையம் சிலம்பில் துஞ்சும்) in two overheard night-tryst poems. The tusker stroking a mate who has just calved (கடுஞ்சூல் ஈன்று ... தைவர) against the tusker that kills a tiger and lies with his mate (உழுவை தொலைச்சி ... பிடிபுணர்ந்து) fits the regret of 328 and the praise of 332. 'Poem of fear' slightly mislabels 328.

352 l.12-16 measures sweetness by a new mode composed by a famed பாண்மகன் for Anji's praise; it says nothing of Avvai or of babble. Purananuru 92's மழலை is Avvai's modest self-description. Only Anji's name links them, and teaches merges the bard's tune with Avvai's poems.

Karikal is in both (376 l.5 கரிகால் காண; 66 l.3 கரிகால் வளவ), and in 376 he is only the onlooker at Atthi's flood-dance at Kazhar. The point is true but thin, and it misses that 66 itself turns the victory against the victor (நின்னினும் நல்லன் அன்றே), which would have given the pair something specific.

The hero-stone rite is shared: 264 l.2-3 மரல்வகுந்து தொடுத்த செம்பூங் கண்ணி ... பெயர்பொறித்து; 269 l.8-11 பல்பெயர் மண்ணி ... ஆர்நார் உரிவையின் செம்பூங் கரந்தை புனைந்த கண்ணி. But it is not 'almost item by item' (no peacock feather; washing and turmeric are new), and in 269 the friend is announcing his return (வந்தனர் விரைந்தே), not filling the heroine's fear of the road.

poems.note: Eyinan, who kept his word 'அஞ்சல்' with his life, is set beside the man who broke his oath, but he is a figure of puram legend, not a native thing; the Atthi and Vanji comparisons are open.

iraicchi.act: at the cow-elephant's cries (மடப்பிடிப் பூசல்) the tusker searches the whirling flood
iraicchi.sense: as the tusker answers his mate's cry through the flood, the lover has come through the cold, dangerous path because her longing called him (படர்ந்த உள்ளம் பழுதுஅன்றாக வந்தனர்).

iraicchi.act: on the omai tree in the waste land the kite calls its mate (பெடைபயிரும்), so as to move pity (அருள்வர)
iraicchi.sense: the foster mother takes comfort that the youth will tend the girl on the road as the kite calls and keeps its mate.

poems.note: The tortoise taking mango fruit with its young (l.15-16) sits inside the place-simile for her hair, so it was not counted.

iraicchi.act: in the drought the tusker stays shrunk beside his starving mate (ஓய்பசிப் பிடியொடு ஒருதிறன் ஒடுங்க)
iraicchi.sense: as the tusker keeps by its mate in hunger, the man who left has great love (பெரும்பேர் அன்பினர்) and will not stay away from her.

poems.note: The elephant pair could be read as heat landscape only; the friend's claim of great love makes the act legible.
The whole poem is an address to the vayalai creeper, so striking it leaves no stated sense.
The bard-woman refusing paddy for pearls belongs to the description of Evvi's town; Anni is an open simile (அன்னி போல).

iraicchi.act: at dusk the flock of herons returns to its nests in the punnai
iraicchi.sense: the birds go home at evening while he, gone for wealth, does not return to her.

poems.note: Ullurai: the stork frightened by the reapers' drum that cries out and shelters in the palm's inner frond pairs with her distressed heart that has gone to rest on his chest.
The lamed ox left alone suffers what the heroine would suffer if left behind, but being left is not an act of a person of the situation.
The oyster-for-toddy barter is part of the Pandya's epithet, and its match to the husband is only one loose pair.

iraicchi.act: the doe licks the stag's back in the yaa tree's striped shade
iraicchi.sense: the doe tending her mate shows him the tenderness he left behind and sharpens his pity for the woman alone at home (நோம்கொல் அளியள்).

poems.note: The colophon says தலைமகள் but the speaker in the camp (பாசறை) worrying about her is plainly the man.
பிடியடி may be the cow-elephant's tracks or the footprint-shaped wells, so no single sense can be named.
Under the alternative colophon the doe is the one addressed, and the doe that sees the net is an open simile (வலைகாண் பிணையின்).
The sleepers and wakers are literal obstacles to the tryst, not images.

iraicchi.act: her mate caught in the boys' net, the hen heron will not eat at dusk, clasps her chick and cries in the palm
iraicchi.sense: as the hen heron grieves alone for her taken mate, the heroine already suffers his absence before marriage, so he should marry her.

poems.note: The peacock frightened by a kanthal cluster that only looks like a snake's hood pairs with the heroine's fear for him on the night path, and the bee freely sipping the flower pairs with the hero who comes and enjoys without regard to that fear; the second pair takes some interpretation.
The tusker with his mate is an open simile (களிற்றின்) for the hero bathing with them, so no sense is left to rise from it.

The fishermen who feast on varal, forget their fishing and sleep pair with the husband who has dallied and neglected his home, and the old woman who still brings them rice at dawn pairs with the wife who is expected to serve him regardless.
